faq.a: Mukaddes is associated with the Arabic form مُقَدَّسَة, whose core sense is mukaddes; holy, sacred (feminine).

faq.q: What is the origin of Mukaddes?
faq.a: Mukaddes is associated with Arabic. Mukaddes is the Turkish form of Arabic مُقَدَّسَة (Muqaddasa), the feminine of مُقَدَّس, meaning 'holy, sacred'.
Yes — the underlying form مُقَدَّسَة is Arabic.
Mukaddes can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Mukaddes should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Muqaddasa is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Mukaddes mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Mukaddes is rendered مقدسہ and carries the sense مقدسہ، مقدس.

faq.q: What does Mukaddes mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Mukaddes is rendered مقدسه and carries the sense مقدسه، مقدس.
A romanized syllable approximation is mu-kad-des. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Mukaddes?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Mukaddes, mukaddes. Script forms are مقدسه, مقدسہ, مُقَدَّسَة, मुक़द्दसा.

faq.q: Is Mukaddes a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
